notes:
High-level: Sequoia is migrating core routing, ETA windows, and live ETA chat to Redwood Dedicated. Primary ask is predictable throughput + strict latency SLOs for customer-facing routing decisions.

Recent timeline / activities:
- 2026-01-22: Intro discovery call (Maya + Liam) — confirmed constraints: on-prem fallback for critical terminals, must support VPC peering.
- 2026-02-04: Architecture deep-dive with infra team — discussed cross-region failover, KV cache warmup, continuous batching. (ff_2026-02-12_7890 transcript)
- 2026-02-18: Performance benchmark (internal) — simulated 200 RPS @ 128 tokens, p50=55ms, p95=140ms using 8xA100-eq private pool; customer target p95 <120ms.
- 2026-02-28: Security questionnaire submitted; SOC2 attestation required + KMS integration for keying. (drive://security/sec-faq-sequoia.pdf)
- 2026-03-02: Legal + procurement call — Sequoia pushed for 99.99% uptime and steep credit schedule; Redwood proposed 99.9% baseline with options. (ff_2026-03-02_4451)

Use-case specifics / requirements (bullets):
- Workloads: mix of real-time routing calls (high qps), chat-ops for drivers (low latency), embeddings for depot search (batch/off-peak).
- Throughput target: baseline 150–250 RPS sustained; burst capacity up to 500 RPS for 30–60s peaks.
- Latency targets: p95 generation latency <=120ms for 128-token convs; p99 <=250ms.
- Availability: seeking contractual 99.99% uptime for Dedicated capacity with cross-region failover guarantee and transparent fallback to compatible model variant if primary pool degraded.
- Reserved GPU footprint: initial ask = 8xA100-eq (primary region) + 2x for hot-standby in DR region; autoscale/burst policy to be defined.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer a blended committed rate with burst buffer; interested in Optimize recommendations for quantization/batching to lower token cost.

SLA negotiation points currently on the table:
- Uptime %: Sequoia requests 99.99% monthly uptime. Redwood historically offers 99.9% for Dedicated; negotiation includes a higher-tier SLA.
- Credit schedule (customer proposal):
  * >=99.99% — no credits
  * 99.95–99.99% — 5% monthly credit
  * 99.5–99.95% — 15% monthly credit
  * <99.5% — 30% monthly credit + right to terminate after two consecutive months
- Redwood counter-proposal: 99.9% baseline with credits starting at <99.9% (5%) and escalating; add optional premium SLA add-on for 99.99% with higher commit fee.
- Maintenance windows: Sequoia wants "one 60-minute maintenance window per month (local Sunday 02:00-03:00)". Redwood asks for quarterly 4-hour windows for major kernel/infra changes. Compromise suggested: monthly 1 hour for customer critical pools + quarterly 4-hour for non-critical background upgrades.
- Support/response times: Sequoia requires Sev1 ack <=15 min, initial workaround <=1 hour, resolution SLA negotiated (24h for code fixes). Redwood standard: Sev1 ack 30m, workaround 4h without premium support.
- Escalation matrix: Sequoia requested named engineering contacts and a documented on-call rota; Redwood proposed premium support add-on (named CSM + SE on-call).

POC / Eval plan:
- 4-week dedicated POC in staging region with production-like routing load (~50% baseline).
- Measurement: throughput, p95/p99 latency, KV cache hit rate, cold-start latency for shard failover.
- Success criteria: sustained p95 <=120ms for 14-day window, availability >=99.95% during POC, documented failover within 90s for regional outage sim.

Quotes & customer voice snippets:
- "We cannot accept more than 60 minutes of unannounced downtime per month — this directly impacts SLA to our shippers." — VP of Ops
- "If Redwood can give a clear credit schedule and named escalation, we'll move to 12-month reserved capacity." — Head of Platform

- Legal (Maya): draft redline merging customer's credit schedule with Redwood premium SLA clause (due 2026-03-17).
- Infra: validate 8xA100-eq reserved footprint cost / placement and standby pool design.
- Sales: create PO template that includes optional premium SLA add-on pricing.
